non_blocking: MOST DAMAGING FAIR OBJECTION (signal detection / eyewitness): the confirmed target-absent effect (H1u, PICK 0.60 vs ISO-any 0.36) is identified only on the UNSOLVED stratum, which is selected on the judge failing, and there both procedures sit near chance (A4: J_PICK +0.03, J_ISO +0.12; A5 ROC curves near the diagonal, dpAUC +0.002 [-0.030,+0.045]). With discriminability near zero, any difference between procedures is a response-bias difference by construction, so the result is 'a which-one-is-correct-or-NONE prompt elicits more commitment than accept/reject prompts when the model cannot tell', not evidence for the eyewitness lineup mechanism (relative judgment under simultaneous presentation). The A4 EACH arm suggests about half the gap is question form rather than joint presentation (fa: ISO 0.32 -> EACH 0.45 -> PICK 0.59; PICK-EACH +0.13 [+0.01,+0.25]). The paper ALREADY ANSWERS most of this honestly: it reports the effect as 'consistent with a criterion shift', says the pick is nearly uninformative, says the ROC test 'has little room to separate them' and that 'a regime of intermediate discriminability would be needed' (main.tex:19, 87, 92), and recommends EACH as an untested mitigation (main.tex:119). What it does not do is run that regime. Experiment that would test it: a 2x2 factorial (presentation: single candidate vs pool of three) x (question: per-candidate verdict vs choose-one-or-NONE, including a single-candidate 'is this correct, or none?' arm), with 1-5 confidence ROCs, on items of intermediate discriminability. The 50 locked but never judged MIXED problems (main.tex:51; exps/c3/strata.json) are exactly that regime and need no new pools; add the Wells removal-without-replacement contrast (choices among the two shared wrong solutions in TA vs TP pools) to test relative judgment directly. A pooled-presentation penalty in J or pAUC there, absent at chance, would support the lineup framing; its absence would reduce the paper to a prompt-criterion effect. Since the paper claims no more than a choosing shift, this limits significance, not correctness.

Unreported self-agreement pathway (my own computation from exps/c3/raw/solve, raw/arms and banks/locked_c3/pools.json, crude string/numeric normalization): in 34 of 90 UNSOLVED TA pools a candidate's final answer matches one of haiku's own two wrong SOLVE answers (1 of 137 SOLVED). PICK chose in 0.71 of those pools vs 0.54 elsewhere (ISO-any 0.41 vs 0.32), and FORCED picked the self-matching candidate in 15 of 34. The PICK-minus-ISO gap (+0.30 vs +0.21) and the H2u inflation (+0.22 vs +0.18) survive in pools without a self-matching answer, so no claim is false, but 'the judge picks what it would itself have answered' is a natural mechanism a reader will raise, and it separates UNSOLVED from SOLVED pools by construction. Report this split.

H3 is pre-registered and reported over all 225 problems, where SOLVED problems (inflation about +0.02) dilute it; the conclusion scopes the claim to 'such problems' (main.tex:119). Recomputed on UNSOLVED only: haiku-pick inflation under haiku verification +0.19, under sonnet +0.16, difference +0.03 [-0.08,+0.15] (n=90). This supports the claim but shows the inflation is largely shared across models, i.e. an item-level 'most plausible wrong solution' effect rather than a same-model pathology; this connects directly to the confidence result of wang2025llms the paper cites (main.tex:35). State the stratum-specific numbers and this reading.

The 'best-looking wrong candidate' wording (main.tex:19) is shown for FORCED (H2u) but not for PICK. It holds for PICK too: on UNSOLVED TA pools where PICK chose (n=54), haiku's isolated acceptance of the chosen solution was 0.43 vs 0.13 for the other two (my computation). One descriptive sentence would close the gap between the abstract's framing and what was tested.

PICK choices on UNSOLVED TA pools by position were 21/10/23 (positions 1/2/3). The paper does not say whether candidate order was randomized or fixed by MathArena order ('first three distinct wrong answers', main.tex:39); state it, since position effects are a known LLM-judge confound and a classic lineup confound.

Novelty versus wang2025llms (COLING 2025) remains the main limit on the score: models choosing among all-wrong options with a no-answer option, and the most confident wrong option nearly matching the correct one, are prior results; the delta here is the pre-registered within-pool comparison against isolated acceptance, the competence stratification and the hit/ROC follow-ups, on one vendor's models with the stratum-by-source confound unresolved (H1 inconclusive, main.tex:73, 116).
